title: Automated Two-dimensional Spatiotemporal Analysis of Mobile Single-molecule FRET Probes
protocol: Install the miniconda Python distribution (minimum required Python version: 3.7).
Open an Anaconda prompt in the Windows Start menu.
Execute `conda activate` if using Linux or macOS.
Enable the community-maintained conda-forge package repository by executing `conda config --add channels conda-forge`.
Set channel priority to strict with `conda config --set channel_priority strict`.
Update all packages with `conda update --all`.
Install required Python packages by executing `conda install opencv trackpy lmfit ipympl scikit-learn pyqt sdt-python jupyterlab`.
Become familiar with JupyterLab, the user interface of the analysis software.
Install the git version control system using the distribution's package management software if on Linux.
Execute `conda install git` to install git otherwise.
Optionally install the sidecar Python package by executing `conda install sidecar`.
Enable EM gain on the EMCCD camera.
Record an image for segmentation if needed.
Excite Fura-2-loaded cells using a 405 nm laser.
Capture emission around 510 nm.
Wait for time tr to permit camera readout.
Choose a small ROI to reduce delay and data size.
Enable frame transfer mode for further reduction of tr.
Alternately excite donor and acceptor fluorophores repeatedly.
Excite the donor for an illumination time till (5-10 ms).
Trigger the camera during donor excitation.
Wait for time tr after donor excitation.
Excite the acceptor while triggering the camera.
Wait for a time tdelay longer than tr.
Repeat steps 2.2.2.1-2.2.2.4.
Choose appropriate tiller and excitation laser intensities.
Record a sufficient number of movies for each sample.
Record a series of randomly placed fiducial markers visible in both emission channels for image registration.
NOTE: Image registration is performed by the software; see step 6.1.4.
Measure the intensity profile for both donor and acceptor excitation light sources for flatfield correction.
Prepare a sample featuring a high density of FRET probes.
Acquire an image upon acceptor excitation.
Photobleach the acceptor.
Record an image upon donor excitation.
Repeat several times in different sample regions.
Prepare a sample decorated with only the donor molecule.
Prepare a second sample decorated with only the acceptor fluorophores.
Record a single-molecule sample of a probe without an acceptor fluorophore to determine donor emission leaking into the acceptor channel.
Acquire recordings of a probe without a donor fluorophore for quantifying direct acceptor excitation by the donor excitation light source.

Record a single-molecule sample featuring two distinct FRET efficiencies to correct for differing detection efficiencies of the donor and acceptor emission channels and differing quantum yields of the dyes.
Choose between a Gaussian fitting algorithm and center-of-mass computation depending on signal density, background, and signal-to-noise ratio.
Download analysis scripts.
Navigate to a folder using the cd command in an Anaconda prompt.
Execute git clone https://github.com/schuetzgroup/fret-analysis.git target_folder.
Replace target_folder with a descriptive name such as 2021-06-14_Force-FRET-experiment.
Copy Jupyter notebooks (01. Tracking.ipynb, 02. Analysis.ipynb, 03. Plots.ipynb) into the newly created folder.
If using the software for the first time, get the Jupyter notebooks from the notebooks subfolder of the root folder.
Start the JupyterLab server by executing jupyter lab in the Anaconda prompt.
Describe datasets.
Load datasets.
Analyze multiple datasets at once if recorded using the same illumination settings.
Assign an identifier to each dataset.
Define patterns that match respective image sequence file names for each dataset.
Specify special purpose datasets, such as fiducial markers for image registration and excitation light profiles for flatfield correction.
Optionally define donor-only and acceptor-only samples for determining correction factors.
Select emission channels in raw images if both were recorded using a single camera.
Use the graphical widget to select appropriate regions for donor and acceptor emissions.
Localize fiducial markers in both emission channels.
Perform image registration.
Find appropriate parameters for localization algorithms for both donor and acceptor emission channels.
Identify randomly distributed fiducial markers across emission channels by the spatial distribution of their nearest neighbors.
Use a custom implementation of an algorithm in sdt-python library to match positions of each marker in the donor emission channel with those in the acceptor emission channel.
Find transformation T mapping coordinates from the donor emission channel to the acceptor emission channel via linear least-squares fit of an affine transformation to markers' positions.
Utilize RANSAC to account for outliers such as wrongly matched positions.

Localize FRET probes independently upon donor and acceptor excitation in all frames and merge results into one table containing frame number, 2-dimensional coordinates, and identifier referring to source image file.
Localize FRET probes upon donor excitation in the sum of images obtained from donor emission ImDD and acceptor emission ImDA.
Localize probes upon acceptor excitation in the acceptor emission channel ImAA.
Perform tracking and fluorescence intensity measurement.
Choose appropriate options for the trackpy36 algorithm used to link FRET probe localizations into trajectories.
Set the maximum search distance from one frame to the next for the trackpy36 algorithm.
Set the number of consecutive frames for which a signal may go undetected using the trackpy36 algorithm.
Determine donor and acceptor excitation light profiles across the field of view from images recorded on a densely labeled sample.
Calculate pixel-by-pixel mean from the images to compute the light profiles.
Subtract camera baseline from the calculated means.
Blur images using a Gaussian filter to reduce effects due to sample impurities.
Divide resulting images pixelwise by their maximum value to get profile p(x,y) mapping coordinates onto the interval [0,1].
Use inspector application to display single-molecule tracks in raw image data and corresponding fluorescence intensities and apparent FRET efficiencies and stoichiometries.
Analyze and filter single-molecule data using 02. Analysis.ipynb Jupyter notebook obtained via 01. Tracking.ipynb notebook.
Discard signals with overlapping point spread functions.
Accept only signals located in well-illuminated regions within the field of view.
Restrict analysis to trajectories present from the beginning of the image sequence for intramolecular FRET studies.
Execute flatfield correction using excitation light source profiles obtained in step 6.1.7.2.
Choose option 1 wherein the acceptor fluorophore bleaches in a single step while the donor shows no partial bleaching.
Reject trajectories where the donor bleaches before the acceptor in a single step for high acceptor photobleaching rates.
Choose option 2 wherein the donor bleaches in a single step while there is no partial acceptor bleaching.
Reject trajectories where the donor bleaches after the acceptor in a single step for high donor photobleaching rates.
Choose option 3 wherein either fluorophore bleaches in a single step while the other does not partially bleach.
Use option 3 for higher flexibility than options 1 and 2, suitable for data analysis with varying conditions.
Choose option 4 wherein donor and acceptor fluorophores show single-step photobleaching or no photobleaching at all.
Prefer option 4 in case of low photobleaching rates to ensure accurate trajectory selection.
Calculate correction factors for donor emission leakage into the acceptor channel α, direct acceptor excitation δ, detection efficiencies γ, and excitation efficiencies β.
Use the calculated correction factors to calculate FRET efficiency E from the apparent efficiency Eapp and stoichiometry S from the apparent stoichiometry Sapp.
Perform further filtering steps.
Select only data points from before the first bleaching event in each trajectory.
Accept only trajectories with at least 75% of data points satisfying 0.35 < S < 0.6.
Perform image segmentation via global or adaptive thresholding methods on auxiliary images.
Create E-S plots to verify that signals of incorrect stoichiometry have been correctly identified and removed.
Plot histograms of FRET efficiencies to provide an overview of the FRET efficiency distributions.
Group the histograms for convenient comparison of results from different experiments.
Evaluate data further using diffusion analysis.
Convert FRET efficiencies to forces in experiments using molecular force sensors.
Perform transition analysis on the data.
Export data in various file formats for use in other analysis software.
